text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball I'm someone who will cheat at something if I can. Like when I was was a kid, and I played [[ASIN:B00000IWCT Monopoly]] with my little brothers, I would steal money from the bank, just because I could.

Each piece of this puzzle has a number on the back of it, and the numbers tell you which pieces fit together. So, it's much easier to flip over all of the pieces of the puzzle, and put it together upside down, that by putting the puzzle together by the picture. And it's much easier by a lot. I think that everyone who does this puzzle will eventually get frustrated, and resort to doing the puzzle upside down, which I consider 'cheating.'

It's very solid, and very strong, when you put it together. The pieces are made of sturdy plastic, not cardboard, like other puzzles. Also the pieces seem like they're cast, or molded, and not cut. That's why the globe surface ends up smooth. But, because all of the pieces were manufactured separately, instead as a whole puzzle, then the picture doesn't always match up from piece to piece.

It comes with a cheap stand, but it looks pretty nice when it's assembled and displayed. I hid a few coins in the middle of it, so it rattles when you move it. It's got lot of area in the middle for a small sphere, so it could double as a secret safe.

Pros:
+Very sturdy, especially when the sphere is completed
+Nice picture, with a bunch of cool zodiac symbols
+High quality

Cons:
-Has numbers on the back of each piece of the puzzle, so it's super simple to assemble
-Plastic, so it doesn't feel like a real puzzle
-The picture doesn't always line up from piece to piece
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball

text_fidelity_a:
White Mountain Puzzles Cereal Boxes - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle [[VIDEOID:71ea1b294d36e01c1968e8869d80c0f7]] I really liked this puzzle. It was a really cool puzzle to put together. There aren't any super easy parts to this puzzle, but there aren't any super difficult parts of this puzzle, either. It was probably medium difficulty all the way through, so this made for a really fun experience throughout the entire puzzle.

This is a piece of art by artist Charlie Girard, which depicts about thirty different cereals. I think that all of the cereal boxes in this art are about thirty or forty years old, and there are many cereals that aren't currently sold today. The artwork is very fun, and this puzzle inspired a lot more conversation than most puzzles do.

I liked how well the puzzle was manufactured. The puzzle back was a really cool dark blue-green color, even though my video doesn't show how awesome the color is. Also, the puzzle pieces were pretty large. Usually puzzle pieces are 0.42 square inches, and these puzzle pieces are 0.72 square inches.

All the cereals in this puzzle are: Twinkles, Wheat Chex, Toasties Corn Flakes, Corn Kix, Corn Bursts, Rice Honeys, Cocoa Krispies, Honey Comb, Sugar Smacks, Alpha-Bits, Frosted Rice, Frosty O's, Raisin Bran, Froot Loops, Sugar Frosted Flakes, Trix, Crispy Critters, Life, Sugar Jets, Sugar Pops, Wheaties, Grape-Nuts Flakes, Apple Jacks, Sugar Sparkled Rice Krinkles, Shredded Wheat, Cap'n Crunch, Corn Flakes, Cheerios, Sugar Crisp, Rice Krispies

Pros:
+High quality puzzle, with a cool color backing
+Large puzzle pieces
+Excellent, fun artwork
+A great conversation starter about memories of different cereals

Cons:
-This puzzle will make you hungry
text_fidelity_b: White Mountain Puzzles Cereal Boxes - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

text_fidelity_a:
Tokaido Board Game (Base Game) | Strategy Game | Travel Adventure Game | Exploration Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 8+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Funforge Simple, serene and elegant, this is a game like few others in your collection. This one is about a trip through Japan, and has very nice Japanese style artwork that really pops. One look at the box cover will tell you how elegant and evocative this game is, and that really is one of it's finest features.

Gameplay is rather simple. Those who rush ahead to see the sights first certainly get some kind of advantage - they often get first choice of where to go - while those who take their time will have plenty of opportunity to catch up, as the last player is always the next to move, meaning that travellers who venture too far out will allow others to make every stop along the way. There are "safe" and predictable options where you always get two or three points, and there are gambling options where you might be able to buy cards that give you far more.

It's a good, simple game that works well as a gateway game, but like many games, it says it's a decent two-player game, and I don't think that it is. It shines with three to four players. The decisions are not particularly deep or exciting, and much of the time, there really are only two choices that you can choose from - move really slow, or move really fast - and those choices are often easy to make.

If you're a gamer, I don't think you'll like this game. You can find better gateway games for sure, and there are thousands of games where you'll make more interesting choices. If you're just getting into games, or if you need something new to play with grandma, then this might be the best choice you can make.
text_fidelity_b: Tokaido Board Game (Base Game) | Strategy Game | Travel Adventure Game | Exploration Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 8+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Funforge

I have flown a pretty nice professional DJI but knew this would not be the same.  It arrived on time and in excellent shape.  First problem was there was only 2 batteries (supposed to be 3).  I charged the batteries (in the garbage charger).  I tried to charge them in my B6 charger but it ready low cell voltage- I should have known then there was an issue.  After assembling everything I took it out and followed the directions to calibrate and sync the drone.  It started up and rose up about 10 feet and started drifting to the right no matter what I did.  I landed it and recalibrated and had the same results.  Then the low battery beeping started.  I landed and changed out batteries (total flight time was less than 5 mins).  The second battery would not even turn on the lights.  Recharged the first battery and in 3 mins the drone crashed with a dead battery.  Charged the second battery again and no go.  So frustrated and disappointed.  I packed it all up and put in for a return.  There are a lot of websites that HIGHLY recommend this drone- I have a feeling they are paid for this as this thing is truly unusable.  The trim functions don't do a darn thing and the batteries are horrible.  Thanks to Amazon for a great hassle free return.
text_fidelity_b: Force1 U45W FPV Drone with Camera for Adults - VR Ready Quadcopter RTF Remote Control Drone with 720p HD Wide Angle Drone Camera, 6 Axis Gyro, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, and 2 Drone Batteries

Goopow Kids Camera Toys for 3-8 Year Old Girls,Children Digital Video Camcorder Camera with Unicorn Soft Silicone Cover, Best Christmas Birthday Festival Gift for Kids - 32G SD Card Included [[VIDEOID:fd8e8c92f2d5416e2ee661d5841a9c4c]] This is definitely a fantastic camera for younger kids. It has a LOT of really great features that will keep this in my son's road-trip arsenal. Picture quality is what you SHOULD expect for this price range. They're fairly grainy in low light, and they aren't exactly cutting edge...but this is FOR YOUNGER KIDS!

Pros:
RUGGED - The camera itself is already rubberized and very thick. THEN it has a thick rubber cover. This is going to hold up against anything my youngest could possibly do to it.
Frames - There are different fun frames and "accessories" to overlay on the photos. Think of this as a kid's version of SnapChat. It's really pretty fun.
Games - There are three included GAMES, and they work surprisingly well for being on a camera. There's Tetris (awesome), Snaker (a Snake clone), and a block moving game. Tetris is fantastic.
Video - Yeah...This shoots video. The camera has a built in mic, too. My son is going to love this...My poor dogs.
MicroSD - Comes bundled with a 32GB MicroSD card. NICE. It also has a USB reader for easy transfer to the computer. Very NICE.
Battery - Rechargeable battery built in. Charges with micro USB cable. Seems to have great battery life compared to other kid's cameras, too. I took pictures over and over...screen stays on. I did pre-view on camera of the different pictures..Took a few videos. One was about five minutes, but the rest were short clips. Battery still going strong.

Cons:
Picture/Video Quality - Fairly standard for a camera in this price range meant for kids. This isn't really a con, as I knew what to expect. I'm including this so people don't think they're getting their kid a professional camera. It's not really a bad thing for me.

Overall, this is a great value. I got this for a six year old, and he is going to be in love with it. It does everything a kid cares about: 1. Looks cool. 2. Takes pictures. 3. Takes Video. 4. text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Kindergarten Math: Amazon Exclusive Kindergarten Math Workbook, Ages 5+ & Hot Dots Let's Master Grade 1 Reading with Talking Pen Very educational with great building-blocks for math success. The actual concepts focused in this activity book are great, but there are two areas of improvement outside of the lessons:

The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Kindergarten Math: Amazon Exclusive Kindergarten Math Workbook, Ages 5+ & Hot Dots Let's Master Grade 1 Reading with Talking Pen

text_fidelity_a:
Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set I have bought three sets of magformers now for all of my grandchildren (3 to 14). Even toddlers can play with them because they are too large to swallow. They also like the solid shapes and colors of Magnatiles but those are more expensive. You can also get magnetic wooden blocks (Tegu) but those are really expensive so I haven't bought any.

The magformers are one of those toys that both kids and adults can sit and play with for an hour or longer. What I've noticed with three young grandkids together is that they each have their favorite pieces and styles of construction. One always creates vehicles, one creates houses, and the third makes towers. The colors and feel of the pieces are both soothing and exciting to work with.

Update: I had five kids and two adults playing with these recently and the person that seemed the most focused on building things is an MIT Neuroscientist. Once he built things following the guide, the kids quickly caught on and followed suit. I recommend that an adult work with the kids to begin with.

Regarding complaints about the magnets not working, if you snap together two piles of similarly shaped objects and then try to put the two piles together, sometimes the piles will reject each other. If you take one pile and start adding it to the other one at a time, all the pieces hold to each other. It seems as though the magnets must change polarity inside the plastic. I'd love a proper explanation.

I only recommend getting sets of 40 or more to have enough pieces to be creative. Wait for them to go on sale unless money is no object. Since all the grandkids took their sets home with them, I've bought a fourth set to keep at my house.

Addendum per request: I first chose these toys because of the brightly colored plastic material but soon discovered that having the pieces snap together and hold their shape is quite satisfying. While they don't take away from the joy of plain wooden blocks, they are different and allow you to vary how you play with them.

This particular kit is right for me because I'll have a crowd of five young children and many adults (thankfully two engineers) for two weeks over Christmas and I'll put this out on a large sofa table in the living room near the tree. That way the kids will feel like they have toys and waiting won't be so hard. It also incorporates many of the other kits you can buy separately so the kids can see specific types of builds.

Go to youtube and type in magformers to see how they are used. Construction is really that easy.
text_fidelity_b: Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set

text_fidelity_a: KINGBOT DeXop Rc Cartoon Car Cartoon Race Car with Music Radio Control Toy Action Figure Rc Vehicle for Toddler, CR04 [[VIDEOID:3cfc56c5d4bf143f7ccc504487426748]] My nephew gets freaked out if his Fischer Price remote control car moves his direction, and he's a brave little kid.  That car goes fairly slowly.  This thing flies and is NOT a toddler toy.  There's no way I'm putting the remote control in the hands an 18 mos. old, even as smart as he is!  The remote offers very little control and that's risky when you have something moving that fast around the floor.  The car doesn't stay on a straight path either.  While moving forward it veers left and right at random and moving backwards is crazy.  The colors are vibrant enough to get a child's attention.  The buttons you push to play sounds are easy to work.  Those are the steering wheel, the driver, and the top of the car.  Pressing the steering wheel causes the cute sound of a car cranking, revving its engine, and rumbling while idle.  The top button causes the weirdest, most random song I've ever heard on a child's toy and it goes on for a solid 36.40 seconds.  Yes, I timed it for this review.  It's that weird a song. When the driver is pressed, the car emits an odd vocalization that sounds like a cross between a dog barking and a man shouting "hey! Hey hey hey! Heeey!" (like something one might hear at the end of a nice Latin dance song) in an odd singsong voice.  The headlights flash whenever a button is pushed and do so for the entirety of whatever sound is playing.  The driver is detachable and once it's pressed down well, it takes some force to get it out.  The overall look of the car and remote is cute, like any regular toddler toy should be.  For an older child who knows how to handle a faster paced remote control car, the price is fair.  As a so called toddler toy...no way am I putting this anywhere near a small child.

Thames & Kosmos Lost Cities: Rivals Card Game | Strategy Auction Adventure | Vibrant Colors for Two to Four Players | Family Friendly Fun by Kosmos This is the third major rendition of the "Lost Cities" games (the card game, the board game, and now Rivals). Each is a game that is ostensibly about discovering lost cities, but is really about putting numbered cards in order. None are special games in my collection, although I now own all three, and all are well-loved by some gamers in the world. Rivals is potentially the most interesting of them, as it introduces a new auction mechanic into the standard put-numbers-in-order formula, but while I found this auction to be a new and interesting method of getting cards, the two other people who I've played it with are not convinced that it's fun so much as it's mean.

I think if you don't mind a game where you play one on one and directly attack others, then this might be something you can handle. I believe that while the others are light-hearted and super easy for anyone to pick up, this suffers from the "meanness" problem, and also from the fact that the more experienced player will easily dispatch newcomers. As many who love Lost CIities have a partner in mind for when they play, and tend not to play with outsiders, this may not be a problem for Rivals, but this is certainly more intense of a "game" than those, and is not always the light hearted fare that the old classics tend to be.

If you want a light, non-interactive card game, then the other Lost Cities are better choices. If you need something more interesting, then this is a good chocie.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Lost Cities: Rivals Card Game | Strategy Auction Adventure | Vibrant Colors for Two to Four Players | Family Friendly Fun by Kosmos

text_fidelity_a:
LolliZ 50 Colored Pencils Set So I read the reviews to these coloring pencils, and saw a lot of rave reviews on them. So I decided to take a chance and purchase them. i haven't even gotten to use them yet when I realized a few of the pencil tips were broken during shipping. When I tried to sharpen a few of them, the lead literally CRUMBLED in the pencil sharpener. There was NO way to sharpen them, as the entire lead was literally just in pieces. Just coming out of the box in this way is NOT a good sign. I am VERY disappointed with these. I nearly ate up quite a few of the pencils just trying to sharpen it. I dunno what everyone was raving about, but I have a pack of cheap cra-z art pencils that are even better than these. These were such a waste of money, and now I am out over $12 for a piece of crap. You can be sure I will be calling Amazon on this item. Unfortunately, I will probably NOT be able to return them, as the box to them literally crumbled when I took them out. I will be reporting THAT to Amazon as well. If you are looking to do some adult coloring like I am, I suggest spending the money on some Marco Raffine pencils. They are a bit pricey, but they are supposed to be worth the money. That will be my next purchase. I am not going to waste my time with the cheap crap anymore.

Update:

After I gave a review of this product, I was contacted by Amazon customer service with an apologetic resolution to send me a replacement set of these pencils to replace the crappie set I originally received. I am happy to report the new set runs more smoothly along the paper & none of the pencils have yet to be eaten up by my electric sharpener. I will say, however, though, that the box they came in literally fell apart before I even took them out of the package they were mailed in, which isn't that big of a problem for me since I put all my pencils upright in a yogurt container anyway for easy access, but for someone who would like to keep them in the box, we'll, good luck with that. My ultimate recommendation is, if you want a really good set of colored pencils, spend the few extra bucks & buy the Marco Raffine 72 pc colored pencils, available thru Amazon. I would recommend them to anyone, & no, I do not get paid or get a discount for saying that.
text_fidelity_b: LolliZ 50 Colored Pencils Set

Hot Wheels Set of 20 Toy Cars & Trucks in 1:64 Scale, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 50 cars is too much at once.

Days as a five year old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 50 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 50 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels Basic Car 50-Pack."

Anthony Trendl
treefortbooks.com

text_fidelity_a: T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle T. S. Shure had a temporary design lapse with this product; probably, the worst coming out of this brand.  Excellent idea coupled with poor execution only increases the frustration one would feel about the product.  The idea of 'magnetic' pieces to help discover countries and continents is great; so is the use of some cutesy imagery that often is often ascribed to a particular country (the dragon shaped like the Great Wall of China is a clear standout).  But trying to cramp all kinds of information in a tiny board proved disastrous.  The pieces are cut with no logic - the sub-continent looks from another planet; the font size for the capitals is so tiny, the target audience will barely notice it;  there are random airplanes and ships distracting the overall map and adding no value.  The tiny pieces are clearly not to be allowed anywhere near babies (it is rated for 6-15 years, to be fair; though it will be a miracle if anyone in that age group will use this for more than a day).  On the positive, with the weak magnetic pull and cardboard-feeling tiny pieces are bound to be lost sooner or later. And then you could create a new game - "which country is missing?".  That may be a better use of this playboard;
text_fidelity_b: T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle

Educational Insights Design & Drill Bolt Buddies Recycling Truck Toy, Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+ The quality is great, and the concept is very creative. We play with this everyday, and think it’s fun, but there’s some thoughts I want to share:

-The clear bolts are somewhat difficult to find on the carpet. I wish the ends (tips) were colored to help make them stand out since they blend into the floor and surfaces.

-The drill bit is always falling out, and it’s also clear, so it can be hard to find it when it falls, and it’s cumbersome to have to keep putting it back in the drill repeatedly.

-The drill has two directions to tighten and loosen the bolts, which is adjusted with the sliding control. The drill itself works very well at tightening and loosening, but it gets a little involved helping my child make adjustments on the drill. My child wants to tighten and loosen a single bolt at a time before moving onto the next bolt, so we’re constantly flip-flopping the controls. Maybe slightly older preschoolers would be more independent using the drill, but I think a manual tool (like a screwdriver) would be the easiest to operate.

Our favorite part of this whole set is dropping all of the bolts in the back of the truck and then opening the hatch to watch all of them tumble out. My child thinks this is hilarious and is by far the best part!

In short, I think this whole set is a great concept, but is slightly overcomplicated. I really feel a simple screwdriver would help simplify the need to shift around buttons constantly, and would even help with dexterity and motor skills more than the cumbersome drill.

Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up I have been enjoying this as a solo game but am happy that it won't be hard to teach friends.

Unlike some games there isn't a finite number of turns...the game ends when someone defeats the boss then each players points are tallied. I like that aspect a lot.

There are some "power" type blocks that benefit all players when one player has success with it.

The art is very cool and whimsical. The paper is sufficient but not very heavy duty. You get plenty of maps...there are 4 of each distinct map design. It's a busy map and I plan on taking the cheapest route possible and using regular sheet protectors and dry erase markers.

I'm not liking the wooden dice at all. For the money I would have really liked some fancier dice. Maybe bigger...maybe more colorful.
You get 4 short presharpened pencils that ...don't have erasers and your first game or two you might need to correct something.

Basically this could have been a print and play. There's nothing at all spectacular about the contents.

My personal little gripe is I don't see how you can be in two places at once. You can attack the map from different sides of the map moving in from starter sections.

That's seems like a lot of negativity but it is a fun little game anyway. You can play it on a small table or most places since there aren't components other than a map and the dice. Also this can encourage people to play who maybe aren't that into games since you don't unload tons of intimidating cards, counters and pieces.

It's a very fine experience. It could've been better for the money though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up

text_fidelity_a:
Wonder Forge Marvel I Can Do That! Game We also have this game in the Dr. Seuss theme, and they're both fun. They're very similar in both cards and directions, but this one is great for little fans of Marvel.

There's a note on the directions page to let you know it's fine to customize the rules for your family. (We tend to do that anyway, but it's a great reminder!) There are 3 stacks of numbered/colored cards(1-red, 2-blue, 3-green). The player turns over one card from each stack. They'll tell the player what to do with which objects. For example, the first card will tell you to "Do a push-up". The second card: "with Captain Marvel's energy ball", and the third card: "on your head". Some tasks are harder than others! Each card will get a certain amount of stars. (At the end of the game, the players will add the stars up. The player with the most wins.) If your child thinks he/she can do the specified task, they will say, "I Can Do That!" If not, they can exchange a card at a time until they feel they can do the task. One of my children was given the task of "Crab walk under the portal, with Spider-Man's web, between your elbows". None of us were talented enough to do that, so he picked again. This is also a great escape route for the shyer(or younger) little ones. Some things will be less embarrassing or more doable for them than others.

There are also "Battle" cards. If one of those are drawn, then any other cards drawn will be put back in the mix. The player will then try to knock down the Green Goblin card with the object specified on the card. If the task is completed, the card is set aside. If not, the player has to put that card in his/her pile as a reminder to discard 2 cards before counting stars at the end of the game. (That way, they can discard to 2 with the lowest number of stars.)

While it may get old with what the players do, it does create a variety of mix and match tasks. The cards are constantly being shuffled. The game ends when all the cards are gone.

This is a great game for when movement is needed. It's not one that the players just sit around and play. The players have to get up and move around. There's also a nice variety of types of objects. There's a plastic block that will need to be filled with air, along with a ball(that's already aired up). There's foam items and thick cardboard objects(Green Goblin and Captain America's shield). My biggest complaint is the "portal". This isn't the sturdiest of things. It's hard to get it to stand up straight, mainly because it has to be rolled up a bit to fit in the box. It makes it hard to get under at times. The bigger/older the child, the harder it will be to crawl under it, either way. This is definitely a game for littler/younger people. Also, I fear that the block won't last long, since objects that require air don't make it too long around my home, in general. (For it to fit back in the box after each game, the air will have to be released. That means you'll have to blow it up before each game. It's not huge, so it's not the biggest deal. Particularly if used in a classroom setting, though, germs/cleaning wipes would be something to put into consideration.)

My children(3, 5, and a tiny 8) have really enjoyed playing this game, though!
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Forge Marvel I Can Do That! Game

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Elefun Snackin Safari Hasbro's new Elefun's Snackin Safari Game for children 3 and up has a wonderful concept for fun, if your child has a lot of patience. The game is made for 1 or 2 players. There are two elephant heads with handles connected to a long slinky trunk with a suction cup on the end. Included are 2 home base cards and 13 snack cards. The object of the game is to pick up a snack card with the suction cup, and there are 3 different ways to play the game.

The first way to play is to find the Golden Tutti Fruit Cake and be the winner. The second way is to collect all your matching colors to win and the third way is to get the most pairs of matching snacks to win. It sounds easy enough, until you realize that it takes a lot of patience to bounce the elephant's slinky trunk quickly and hard enough to actually suction a card to it. It could take 6 times or 60 times, as the slinky is a weak plastic one and the small suction cup needs to be pushed on a card to pick it up.

Surprisingly enough, the little ones loved the concept, but after a dozen tries to pick up a card, became frustrated. If Hasbro can tweak this game to make a stronger slinky and stronger suction cup, so the little ones can pick up a card after a few tries, this game would be a big hit. I hope Hasbro reads these reviews and makes this cute game less frustrating, as the kids will really enjoy it!
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Elefun Snackin Safari

While I would have loved (although not necessarily expected) some karate-chop action in the parent figures, or flamethrower accessories, this is a pretty cool looking fortress, no wait, I mean dollhouse, and my daughter loves it, even if she doesn't understand why GI Joe keeps trying to rappel up to the 4th floor balcony with his grappling hook. .

Seriously though, she really does love this dollhouse. I think it's pretty good for the price, as it's absolutely huge (close to 3 ft tall), but to be honest, I expected a lot more in terms of the "stuff" inside. There is some detail built into the walls, but hardly any furniture pieces that you can move around. There are some family members included, but only parents and baby, who appears to have just come from the hospital. It's a bit like a family just moving into their first apartment, where all they have is a moldy old sofa and some flowers on the wall.

Everything that she wants to play with is, of course, something I have to buy separately. That's a bit annoying, but typical I suppose, although someone with more experience in these sorts of girl-fortresses might know of a better alternative. Practically speaking, Cobra Commander and Skelator could just waltz right in the front door, as there are no missile launchers, so those must come in one of the accessory packs.

text_fidelity_a:
Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit I am a Lego fan, but I kept that in mind as I reviewed this, not wanting it to make my review unfair.
So, lets start with the kit. The pieces do not fit together as well as Lego pieces do. That’s not a huge thing, but it’s a little annoying with some of the steps.
I have to say that the instructions are much better than Lego ones –MegaBlox devised a very clear way to show what piece to put, and where to put it. That was nice. However, they lace the style Lego shows – if this were a Lego set, it would be hollow – allowing things to go inside it – this set is solid, no room inside for anything. The feet fall off easily, which gets old fast.

Plus there are many “special” bricks that will limit the owners ability to make other things out of the set. Although, that is moot if you have a sizable MegaBlox collection already.

The finished piece is nice – a little boxy – think Minions meets Minecraft.

My issue is the price though. If you look at Lego sets (aside from brand ones like Disney and some of the collectable ones) the cost is around 10c per brick.
This set works out at almost 30cents per brick. Three times the cost of a comparably sized Lego set.
The quality does not warrant that price. Despite the added value of the Despicable Me brand. If it was rounder, more interactive, or had stronger feet I would be inclines to give it a better score

If the shortcomings don’t bother you, and your life *needs* all things “Despicable Me” then you will enjoy this.
If someone else is paying for it, you will find it a bargain.

Otherwise I would recommend you get your Despicable Me and building set fix from a better product.
text_fidelity_b: Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit

However, my two and a half year old grandson and eleven month old granddaughter both love to watch the flow and manipulating the timers. It definitely is soothing to observe and the smooth rounded design with tapered centers makes it safe and easy to handle for even young children.
I’m a retired early childhood teacher and would love to get one of these that flowed for two or three minutes to use as a timer for “thinking time” when my toddler needs to regroup due to inappropriate behavior.
That being said, it is fun and as an interactive “toy” I’d give it a thumbs up!

The kitchen itself is made of a high grade, colorful and sturdy plastic that you have to put together with a screwdriver. You'll spend around a half hour screwing the walls and shelves together and to the base, and that's it. The batteries that make Dora talk to the little cook are already included and inserted in the compartment.

This colorful kitchen is very compact and everything gets conveniently stored inside the roomy refrigerator and oven. The sink is over the refrigerator and the burner and grill is over the oven. Above the sink/stove top is a window and a place to slide in the recipe card, and above this at the top is a shelf. Next to the recipe card is a cell phone holder. Dora stands behind the stove cooktop to the other side.

The recipe card is double sided, with 2 recipes on each side for a total of 4 recipes included. When you slide the card in, you can then press one of two flower buttons that speak to you with directions for your recipe. Sometimes the phone will ring as well and speak to you. There are over 60 phrases in English and Spanish. One side of the card has 2 recipes for a Barbecue- hamburgers and ice cream and the other side of the card has 2 recipes for a Spring Picnic- huevos rancheros and tacos. Step by step, Dora tells the little cook exactly what to do.

All the ingredients and cooking utensils your little chef will need to create these 4 recipes are included. There are 20 play accessories, including: plate, spatula, pan, cup, fork, spoon, phone, salad dressing, milk, hash browns, egg, lettuce, hamburger patty, tortilla, chicken breast, buns, banana and ice creams. Some of the food items are hard plastic and some softer, like the real food.

Your kids will have so much fun learning to create scrumptious dishes with Dora in this wonderful talking kitchen. I'm already looking for more recipe cards for this kitchen and I found a great Holiday Cookies one for this Christmas for them. We've had other play kitchens, but this talking one gets all the play time by both the girls and boys.

text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) I'm just combining my thoughts on the various guns and products into one review, in case anyone would like to do a bit of comparing in one spot.

Darts:

The darts are kind of like a third of a straw, with a cool rubber-like tip. These tips ONLY stick to the special targets, which are on the shields(both the wearable ones and the ones that attach to the guns). There are also targets that stick to the wall. (I just taped the top of these targets, as opposed to sticking the whole thing on the wall.) We tested these out on mirrors and windows. They really don't stick to anything, but the special targets.

They're mostly bright colored, which makes it easier to find them once they've been shot. You'll have to take several time outs just to gather darts.

This company has made it perfectly clear that these darts are NOT made for little ones. I just want to reinforce that. I have an 18 month old that puts things in his mouth constantly. We found a large rock in his poo diaper. :S These are simply irresistible to him with their chewy rubber tip. He's chewed the tops off a few of them, even when we were trying to keep a close eye on him. The tops DO come off when chewed on, so these are definitely a choking hazard for little ones.

I try to teach our boys to never aim a gun at anyone, but I've been hit with a few of the darts. One hurt, but the others didn't. I think it depends on how close the gun is, and simply how the dart hits a person. In general, they don't seem to hurt too much.

Other than chewing, they seem pretty sturdy, though. They're had lots of use and bending, but they still work in the guns.

Farshot Blaster:

This is the smallest gun in this line(that we have...there seems to be a smaller "clipfire"). You pull back the top to "pump it up". It will only hold 1 dart at a time for shooting, but 2 spares fit in the bottom of the gun.

This gun is the easiest to aim, as far as target practice, and if that's what you'd like it for, I'd recommend this one. I've found it to be a great stress reliever. When the little ones are creating chaos, I can pull out this gun, tape a target to the wall, and do a little target practice.

Twisted Spinner Blaster:

This is the medium sized gun in this line. To shoot it, you pull an arm on the gun back towards yourself. The darts are loaded in the round end. It will hold 8 darts. As with all the guns, it comes with removable shields.

This one is a little harder to aim, but it's still fun.

Rapid Madness Blaster:

This is the largest gun in this line. You push and pull an arm to pump it up. The trigger is super sensitive, so it takes a couple of seconds to shoot all 20 darts that it holds. Those darts are held in a clip that slides into the side of the gun. This one is the most fun, BUT you don't get much shooting time before having to round up darts.

Bandolier:

This is an adjustable strap that you can wear across your body. It has a special target that the darts will stick to. It will also hold 12 extra darts.

Eye goggles:

These are pretty cool. As advertised, they won't fog up. They're made of a thick-like plastic/rubber, and give you "bug vision". They're also adjustable. My little ones are younger than the recommended age, but the clip kept coming off with them, and we put the goggles back together so much that I wanted to throw them away. Still, I don't think adults will have that problem, and they really are pretty cool!

Targets:

These are a little smaller than I prefer, but they do come in slightly different sizes and shapes. You get different points for different areas. The darts DO stick really well to these targets, and ONLY these targets, but if the dart hits wrong, it still won't stick. I'd say our darts stuck about half the time with the larger guns, and about 3/4th of the time with the farshot blaster. You can peel the back off and it will stick to the wall/door, but as I mentioned above, I just taped it instead. They're a fun way to create a little "battle" zone in one's room, or just simple target practice.

Overall, we've had tons of fun with these guns, and just think they're all pretty awesome.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

Loopdedoo – DIY Friendship Bracelet Maker Kit – Make Bracelets in Minutes – Award-Winning Craft Kit - Ages 8+ Mixed feelings on this one.

It can maybe speed up wrapping bracelets, necklaces, etc. But it also requires some patience and if you try to go too fast, you're just going to make a mess of things. So, honestly, you won't be going much faster than if doing this by hand. If you want a thicker cord it can be tricky to fit it through the holding slot (tip - instead of going through the slot on the top, go through the bottom).

Making anything longer than a bracelet will also take some serious patience and practice as it requires sliding your work up and therefore tying your already worked piece into place / slide it through the holding slot.

Once you get the hang of it, it does feel like this is almost a third hand. It's a great way to manage the cords while you work but it's definitely not going to be worth it for most people. It doesn't feel like the game changer that their Loopdeloom did. For me it's helpful as I do have problems with my hands at times.
